{{山系 |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = <small>{{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰}}。<br/>左から {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山}}。</small> |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県}}{{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}}
'''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス}}.
== Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山}}.
The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市}}.
The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.<ref>{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}</ref><ref>{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}}</ref>
== Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山}} (501 m)
* Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山}} (320 m)
== Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|ja|宇都宮二荒山神社}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市}} located to the northwest of the range.

{{山系 |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = <small>{{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰}}。<br/>左から {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山}}。</small> |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県}}{{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}}
'''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス}}.
== Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山}}.
The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市}}.
The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.<ref>{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}</ref><ref>{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}}</ref>
== Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山}} (501 m)
* Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山}} (320 m)
== Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|ja|宇都宮二荒山神社}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市}} located to the northwest of the range.

{{山系 |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = <small>{{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰}}。<br/>左から {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山}}。</small> |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県}}{{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}}
'''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス}}.
== Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山}}.
The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市}}.
The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.<ref>{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}</ref><ref>{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}}</ref>
== Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山}} (501 m)
* Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山}} (320 m)
== Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|ja|宇都宮二荒山神社}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市}} located to the northwest of the range.

''' ''' {{山系 |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=draft}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = {{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー|12=draft}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=draft}}。
左から {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=draft}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=draft}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|12=draft}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=draft}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|12=draft}}{{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|12=draft}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|12=draft}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|12=draft}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|12=draft}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=draft}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川|12=draft}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=draft}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|12=draft}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮|12=draft}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=draft}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=draft}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=draft}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=draft}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|12=draft}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=draft}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|12=draft}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山|12=draft}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=draft}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=draft}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=draft}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=draft}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山|12=draft}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|12=draft}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道|12=draft}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号|12=draft}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|12=draft}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=draft}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=draft}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=draft}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|12=draft}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|12=draft}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=draft}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=draft}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|12=draft}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=draft}} (501 m) * Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=draft}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=draft}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山|12=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|12=draft}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=draft}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|12=draft}} (320 m) == Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|12=draft}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|ja|宇都宮二荒山神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|12=draft}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|12=draft}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|12=draft}} located to the northwest of the range. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=[[栃木県立博物館|ja|栃木県立博物館]] 編|title=こんなにあるよ!とちぎの鉱物 ～鉱山と鉱物のものがたり～|date=2014-07-19|publisher={{ill|Tochigi Prefectural Museum|ja|栃木県立博物館|12=draft}}|series=第109回企画展|page=80|isbn=978-4-88758-077-0|ref={{sfnref|栃木県立博物館 編|2014}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|title=地域総合調査報告 篠井|publisher={{ill|Utsunomiya Chuo Girls' High School|ja|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校|12=draft}}社会部|date=1977-02-15|page=43|ref={{sfnref|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977}}}} === Related Articles === * {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|12=draft}} * {{ill|Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|ja|宇都宮二荒山神社|12=draft}} * {{ill|Hachimanyama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|12=draft}} * {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=draft}} * {{ill|Myōjin-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|12=draft}} ''' ''' {{山系 |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=draft}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = {{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー|12=draft}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=draft}}。
左から {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=draft}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=draft}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|12=draft}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=draft}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|12=draft}}{{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|12=draft}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|12=draft}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|12=draft}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|12=draft}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=draft}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川|12=draft}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=draft}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|12=draft}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮|12=draft}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=draft}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=draft}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=draft}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=draft}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|12=draft}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=draft}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|12=draft}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山|12=draft}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=draft}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=draft}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=draft}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=draft}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山|12=draft}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|12=draft}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道|12=draft}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号|12=draft}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|12=draft}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=draft}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=draft}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=draft}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|12=draft}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|12=draft}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=draft}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=draft}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|12=draft}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=draft}} (501 m) * Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=draft}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=draft}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山|12=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|12=draft}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=draft}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|12=draft}} (320 m) == Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|12=draft}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|ja|宇都宮二荒山神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|12=draft}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|12=draft}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|12=draft}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|12=draft}} located to the northwest of the range. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=draft}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川|12=draft}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=draft}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|12=draft}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮|12=draft}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=draft}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=draft}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=draft}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=draft}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|12=draft}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=draft}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|12=draft}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山|12=draft}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=draft}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=draft}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=draft}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=draft}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山|12=draft}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|12=draft}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道|12=draft}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号|12=draft}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|12=draft}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=draft}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=draft}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=draft}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|12=draft}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|12=draft}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=draft}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=draft}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|12=draft}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=draft}} (501 m) * Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=draft}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=draft}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山|12=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|12=draft}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=draft}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|12=draft}} (320 m) == Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|12=draft}}. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=draft}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|12=draft}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山|12=draft}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=draft}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=draft}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=draft}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=draft}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山|12=draft}}. 左から {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=draft|12=draft}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=draft|12=draft}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|12=draft|12=draft}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=draft|12=draft}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|12=draft|12=draft}}{{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|12=draft|12=draft}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|12=draft|12=draft}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|12=draft|12=draft}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=draft|12=draft}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川|12=draft|12=draft}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=draft|12=draft}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|12=draft|12=draft}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮|12=draft|12=draft}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=draft|12=draft}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=draft|12=draft}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=draft|12=draft}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=draft|12=draft}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|12=draft|12=draft}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=draft|12=draft}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|12=draft|12=draft}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山|12=draft|12=draft}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=draft|12=draft}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=draft|12=draft}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=draft|12=draft}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=draft|12=draft}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山|12=draft|12=draft}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|12=draft|12=draft}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号|12=draft|12=draft}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|12=draft|12=draft}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=draft|12=draft}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=draft|12=draft}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=draft|12=draft}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|12=draft|12=draft}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|12=draft|12=draft}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=draft|12=draft}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=draft|12=draft}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|12=draft|12=draft}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=draft|12=draft}} (501 m) * Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=draft|12=draft}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=draft|12=draft}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山|12=draft|12=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=draft|12=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|12=draft|12=draft}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=draft|12=draft}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|12=draft|12=draft}} (320 m) == Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|12=draft|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|12=draft|12=draft}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|ja|宇都宮二荒山神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|12=draft|12=draft}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|12=draft|12=draft}} located to the northwest of the range. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * ''' ''' {{山系 |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = {{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー|qq=draft|qq=draft}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}。
左から {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (501 m) * Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (320 m) == Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|ja|宇都宮二荒山神社|1=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located to the northwest of the range. == Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (501 m) * Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (320 m) == Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|ja|宇都宮二荒山神社|1=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located to the northwest of the range. == {{山系 |名称=篠井富屋連峰 |画像=[[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |画像キャプション=[[宇都宮タワー]]から見た篠井富屋連峰。
左から榛名山、男山、本山、飯盛山、兜山、482mピーク、黒戸山、高館山、矢倉山。手前の緑は[[八幡山 (宇都宮市)|八幡山]]と[[戸祭山]]。 |所在地=[[栃木県]][[宇都宮市]] |最高峰=[[本山 (宇都宮市)|本山]] |標高=561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=本山の位置|width=256}} '''篠井富屋連峰'''（しのいとみやれんぽう）は、[[栃木県]][[宇都宮市]]北部山系を成す山域の総称である。南東側に[[田川 (利根川水系)|田川]]、北西側に[[鬼怒川]]が流れ、両川に挟まれた形で山地が形成されている。'''宇都宮アルプス'''と呼ばれることもある。 == 概要 == [[栃木県]]北西部山系は[[日光二荒山神社]]や[[日光東照宮]]を祀る[[日光山内]]から[[小倉山 (日光市)|小倉山]]、[[愛宕山 (日光市)|愛宕山]]、[[茶臼山 (日光市)|茶臼山]]、[[浅間山 (日光市)|浅間山]]と連なり、宇都宮市北部で'''篠井富屋連峰'''を経て宇都宮市街部の[[戸祭山]]、[[八幡山 (宇都宮市)|八幡山]]、[[明神山 (宇都宮市)|明神山]]と続く。 篠井富屋連峰の最高峰は'''本山'''で、標高は561.6mである。[[本山 (宇都宮市)|本山]]の北側には'''高へら山'''（標高432.8m）があってその先には平坦部を挟んで日光市境を跨いで丸山（標高326.2m）、堂室山（標高305.9m）に続く。本山の南側に篠井富屋連峰の山並みが続く。まず本山の南側には'''飯盛山'''（標高501m）があり、その南東側には'''高舘山'''（標高476.6m）が続く。高舘山から北東に向かう峰の先には'''矢倉山'''（標高409m）、東に向かう低い峰の先には'''妙見山'''（標高320m）、そして南に向かう峰の先には'''黒戸山'''（標高412m）に続き'''兜山'''（標高372m）があり、その南側に[[東北自動車道]]および[[国道293号]]を挟んで'''笠松山'''（標高327.8m）がある。さらに高館山の西側には'''雷電山'''（標高368m）があって、その北西に'''寅巳山'''（標高458.8m）があり、そして日光市の浅間山に続いていく。 篠井連峰の一帯は、[[篠井金山]]（富屋鉱山）として{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}[[金]]や[[銅]]を採掘していた{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}}。 == 主な山 == * 篠井連峰 ** 本山（561.6m） ** 男山（527m） ** 榛名山（524m） ** 飯盛山（501m） * 富屋連峰 ** 高館山（476.6m） ** 黒戸山（412m） ** 鬼山（372m） ** 兜山（372m） ** 笠松山（327.8m） ** 矢倉山（409m） ** 妙見山（320m） == 周辺 == 篠井富屋連峰は日光山系と[[宇都宮丘陵]]の間にある山地帯であり、この山地一帯は古くより山岳信仰の対象となり、[[宇都宮二荒山神社]]や[[塙田八幡宮]]、[[智賀都神社]]、高尾神社、薬師堂、大日大権現堂などの寺社が置かれ、[[日光市]]内の愛宕神社、さらに日光山内の寺社群なども篠井富屋連峰の北西の先に所在する。 == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=[[栃木県立博物館]] 編|title=こんなにあるよ!とちぎの鉱物 ～鉱山と鉱物のものがたり～|date=2014-07-19|publisher=栃木県立博物館|series=第109回企画展|page=80|isbn=978-4-88758-077-0|ref={{sfnref|栃木県立博物館 編|2014}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|title=地域総合調査報告 篠井|publisher=[[栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校]]社会部|date=1977-02-15|page=43|ref={{sfnref|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977}}}} == 関連項目 == * [[宇都宮市]] * [[宇都宮二荒山神社]] * [[八幡山 (宇都宮市)]] * [[戸祭山]] * [[明神山 (宇都宮市)]] {{DEFAULTSORT:しのいとみやれんほう}} [[Category:山岳名目録]] [[Category:栃木県の山]] [[Category:栃木県の自然景勝地]] [[Category:宇都宮市の地理]] [[Category:うつのみや百景]]

''' ''' {{山系 |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = {{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー|qq=draft|qq=draft}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}。
左から {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Yakushi-dō, ''' ''' {{山系 |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = {{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー|qq=draft|qq=draft}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}。
左から {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (501 m) * Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (320 m) == Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|ja|宇都宮二荒山神社|1=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located to the northwest of the range. == 左から {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (327.8 m). ''' ''' {{山系 |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|qq=}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = {{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Tower|qq=}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|qq=}}。
左から {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haruna-yama|qq=}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|qq=}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|qq=}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|qq=}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|qq=}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|qq=}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|qq=}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|qq=}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|qq=}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|qq=}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tochigi Prefecture|qq=}}{{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya City|qq=}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|qq=}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya City|ja|宇都宮市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya City|qq=}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tochigi Prefecture|qq=}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa (Tone River system)|qq=}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa|ja|鬼怒川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinugawa|qq=}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Alps|qq=}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tochigi Prefecture|qq=}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|ja|日光二荒山神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Tōshō-gū|qq=}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountains|qq=}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogura-yama|qq=}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago-yama|qq=}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chausu-yama|qq=}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asama-yama|qq=}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|qq=}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|qq=}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|qq=}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin-yama|qq=}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|qq=}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahera-yama|qq=}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō City|qq=}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|ja|丸山|lt=Maruyama|lt_ja=丸山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maruyama|qq=}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōshitsu-yama|qq=}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|qq=}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|qq=}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|qq=}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|lt=Myoken-yama|lt_ja=妙見山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myoken-yama|qq=}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|qq=}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|qq=}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tohoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tohoku Expressway|qq=}} and {{ill|National Route 293|ja|国道293号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Route 293|qq=}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|qq=}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|qq=}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raiden-yama|qq=}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torami-yama|qq=}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō City|qq=}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|qq=}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|qq=}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|qq=}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Haruna-yama|ja|榛名山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haruna-yama|qq=}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|qq=}} (501 m) * Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|qq=}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|qq=}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oniyama|qq=}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|qq=}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|qq=}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|qq=}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Myoken-yama|ja|妙見山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myoken-yama|qq=}} (320 m) == Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountain system|qq=}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Hills|qq=}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|ja|宇都宮二荒山神社|1=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chigato Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takao Shrine|qq=}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō City|ja|日光市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō City|qq=}} located to the northwest of the range. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == *
