左から [[:en:Mount Haruna|Haruna-yama]], {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|1=Otokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11578139}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24887668}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Mount Tomatsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}。 |所在地 = [[:en:Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi Prefecture]][[:en:Utsunomiya|Utsunomiya City]] |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of [[:en:Utsunomiya|Utsunomiya City]] in [[:en:Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi Prefecture]]. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa (Tone River system)|1=Tagawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576724}}, and on its northwest side the [[:en:Kinugawa River|Kinugawa]] runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Alps|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 篠井富屋連峰|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of [[:en:Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi Prefecture]] stretches from the area within the [[:en:Futarasan shrine|Nikkō Futarasan Shrine]] and [[:en:Nikkō Tōshō-gū|Nikkō Tōshō-gū]] enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountains|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日光の社寺|1=Shrines and Temples of Nikkō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1063133}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chausu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asama-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Mount Tomatsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin-yama|1=Mount Myōjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11512579}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahera-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of [[:en:Nikkō|Nikkō City]], are [[:en:Maruyama|Maruyama]] (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōshitsu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 高館山|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while a low peak to the east leads to [[:en:Mount Myōken|Myoken-yama]]. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, and to the south, separated by the [[:en:Tōhoku Expressway|Tohoku Expressway]] and [[:en:Japan National Route 293|National Route 293]], is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|1=Kasamatsuyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11599914}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raiden-yama|1=Raiden-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11660213}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torami-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of [[:en:Nikkō|Nikkō City]]. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|1=Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q99484649}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24887668}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|1=Otokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11578139}} (527 m) ** [[:en:Mount Haruna|Haruna-yama]] (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}} (501 m) * Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oniyama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|1=Kasamatsuyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11599914}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (409 m) ** [[:en:Mount Myōken|Myoken-yama]] (320 m) == Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountain system|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Hills|qq=}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as [[:en:Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine]], {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|1=Hanawada Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11428387}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chigato Shrine|1=Chigata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q98526762}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takao Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in [[:en:Nikkō|Nikkō City]] located to the northwest of the range. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=[[栃木県立博物館|ja|栃木県立博物館]] 編|title=こんなにあるよ!とちぎの鉱物 ～鉱山と鉱物のものがたり～|date=2014-07-19|publisher=[[:en:Tochigi Prefectural Museum|Tochigi Prefectural Museum]]|series=第109回企画展|page=80|isbn=978-4-88758-077-0|ref={{sfnref|栃木県立博物館 編|2014}}}} * {{Cite 栃木県立宇都宮中央高等学校|1=Tochigi Prefectural Utsunomiya Chuo High School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11535235}}社会部|date=1977-02-15|page=43|ref={{sfnref|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977}}}} === Related Articles === * [[:en:Utsunomiya|Utsunomiya City]] * [[:en:Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine]] * {{ill|Hachimanyama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 [[arz:جبال شينوى توميا]][[ja:篠井富屋連峰]] [[arz:جبال شينوى توميا]][[ja:篠井富屋連峰]] [[arz:جبال شينوى توميا]][[ja:篠井富屋連峰]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11603531]] Wikidata name: Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:23, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} ''' ''' {{Infobox Mountain |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = {{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Tower|1=Utsunomiya Tower|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11449698}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}。
左から {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Haruna-yama}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|1=Otokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11578139}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24887668}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Mount Tomatsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}{{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa (Tone River system)|1=Tagawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576724}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa River|en|Kinugawa River|WD=Q1042040|lt=Kinugawa}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Alps|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 篠井富屋連峰|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Futarasan shrine|en|Futarasan shrine|WD=Q701927|lt=Nikkō Futarasan Shrine}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|en|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountains|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日光の社寺|1=Shrines and Temples of Nikkō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1063133}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chausu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asama-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Mount Tomatsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin-yama|1=Mount Myōjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11512579}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahera-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|en|Maruyama|WD=Q1739153|lt=Maruyama}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōshitsu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 高館山|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Mount Myōken|en|Mount Myōken|WD=Q868348|lt=Myoken-yama}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|en|Tōhoku Expressway|WD=Q428428|lt=Tohoku Expressway}} and {{ill|Japan National Route 293|en|Japan National Route 293|WD=Q6157155|lt=National Route 293}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|1=Kasamatsuyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11599914}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raiden-yama|1=Raiden-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11660213}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torami-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|1=Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q99484649}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24887668}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|1=Otokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11578139}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}} (476.6 m) ** Shrine|ja|高尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takao Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the [[arz:جبال شينوى توميا]][[ja:篠井富屋連峰]] [[arz:جبال شينوى توميا]][[ja:篠井富屋連峰]] [[arz:جبال شينوى توميا]][[ja:篠井富屋連峰]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11603531]] Wikidata name: Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:23, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} ''' ''' {{Infobox Mountain |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = {{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Tower|1=Utsunomiya Tower|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11449698}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}。
左から {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Haruna-yama}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|1=Otokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11578139}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24887668}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Mount Tomatsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}{{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa (Tone River system)|1=Tagawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576724}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa River|en|Kinugawa River|WD=Q1042040|lt=Kinugawa}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Alps|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 篠井富屋連峰|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Futarasan shrine|en|Futarasan shrine|WD=Q701927|lt=Nikkō Futarasan Shrine}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|en|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountains|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日光の社寺|1=Shrines and Temples of Nikkō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1063133}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chausu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asama-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Mount Tomatsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin-yama|1=Mount Myōjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11512579}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahera-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|en|Maruyama|WD=Q1739153|lt=Maruyama}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōshitsu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 高館山|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Mount Myōken|en|Mount Myōken|WD=Q868348|lt=Myoken-yama}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|en|Tōhoku Expressway|WD=Q428428|lt=Tohoku Expressway}} and {{ill|Japan National Route 293|en|Japan National Route 293|WD=Q6157155|lt=National Route 293}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|1=Kasamatsuyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11599914}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raiden-yama|1=Raiden-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11660213}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torami-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|1=Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q99484649}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major [[arz:جبال شينوى توميا]][[ja:篠井富屋連峰]] [[arz:جبال شينوى توميا]][[ja:篠井富屋連峰]] [[arz:جبال شينوى توميا]][[ja:篠井富屋連峰]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11603531]] Wikidata name: Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:23, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} ''' ''' {{Infobox Mountain |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = {{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Tower|1=Utsunomiya Tower|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11449698}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}。
左から {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Haruna-yama}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|1=Otokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11578139}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24887668}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Mount Tomatsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}{{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa (Tone River system)|1=Tagawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576724}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa River|en|Kinugawa River|WD=Q1042040|lt=Kinugawa}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Alps|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 篠井富屋連峰|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Futarasan shrine|en|Futarasan shrine|WD=Q701927|lt=Nikkō Futarasan Shrine}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|en|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountains|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日光の社寺|1=Shrines and Temples of Nikkō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1063133}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chausu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asama-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Mount Tomatsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin-yama|1=Mount Myōjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11512579}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahera-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|en|Maruyama|WD=Q1739153|lt=Maruyama}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōshitsu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 高館山|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Mount Myōken|en|Mount Myōken|WD=Q868348|lt=Myoken-yama}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|en|Tōhoku Expressway|WD=Q428428|lt=Tohoku Expressway}} and {{ill|Japan National Route 293|en|Japan National Route 293|WD=Q6157155|lt=National Route 293}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|1=Kasamatsuyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11599914}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raiden-yama|1=Raiden-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11660213}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torami-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|1=Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q99484649}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24887668}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|1=Otokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11578139}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Haruna-yama}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}} (501 m) * Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oniyama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|1=Kasamatsuyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11599914}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Mount Myōken|en|Mount Myōken|WD=Q868348|lt=Myoken-yama}} (320 m) == Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountain system|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Hills|qq=}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|en|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|WD=Q10946254|lt=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|1=Hanawada Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11428387}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chigato Shrine|1=Chigata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q98526762}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takao Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}} located to the northwest of the range. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=[[栃木県立博物館|ja|栃木県立博物館]] [[arz:جبال شينوى توميا]][[ja:篠井富屋連峰]] [[arz:جبال شينوى توميا]][[ja:篠井富屋連峰]] [[arz:جبال شينوى توميا]][[ja:篠井富屋連峰]] ''' ''' {{Infobox Mountain |名称 = {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}} |image = [[File:Peaks_of_the_Shinois_and_Tomiyas_viewing_from_Utsunomiya_Tower.jpg|300px]] |imageキャプション = {{ill|Utsunomiya Tower|ja|宇都宮タワー|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Tower|1=Utsunomiya Tower|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11449698}}から見た{{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}。
左から {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Haruna-yama}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|1=Otokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11578139}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24887668}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Mount Tomatsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}{{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa (Tone River system)|1=Tagawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576724}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa River|en|Kinugawa River|WD=Q1042040|lt=Kinugawa}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Alps|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 篠井富屋連峰|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Futarasan shrine|en|Futarasan shrine|WD=Q701927|lt=Nikkō Futarasan Shrine}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|en|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountains|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日光の社寺|1=Shrines and Temples of Nikkō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1063133}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chausu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asama-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Mount Tomatsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin-yama|1=Mount Myōjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11512579}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahera-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|en|Maruyama|WD=Q1739153|lt=Maruyama}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōshitsu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 高館山|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Mount Myōken|en|Mount Myōken|WD=Q868348|lt=Myoken-yama}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|en|Tōhoku Expressway|WD=Q428428|lt=Tohoku Expressway}} and {{ill|Japan National Route 293|en|Japan National Route 293|WD=Q6157155|lt=National Route 293}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|1=Kasamatsuyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11599914}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raiden-yama|1=Raiden-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11660213}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torami-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|1=Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q99484649}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24887668}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|1=Otokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11578139}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Haruna-yama}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}} (501 m) * Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oniyama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|1=Kasamatsuyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11599914}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Mount Myōken|en|Mount Myōken|WD=Q868348|lt=Myoken-yama}} (320 m) == Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountain system|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Hills|qq=}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|en|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|WD=Q10946254|lt=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|1=Hanawada Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11428387}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chigato Shrine|1=Chigata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q98526762}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takao Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}} located to the northwest of the range. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=[[栃木県立博物館|ja|栃木県立博物館]] 編|title=こんなにあるよ!とちぎの鉱物 ～鉱山と鉱物のものがたり～|date=2014-07-19|publisher={{ill|Tochigi Prefectural Museum|en|Tochigi Prefectural Museum|WD=Q11535226|lt=Tochigi Prefectural Museum}}|series=第109回企画展|page=80|isbn=978-4-88758-077-0|ref={{sfnref|栃木県立博物館 編|2014}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|title=地域総合調査報告 篠井|publisher={{ill|Utsunomiya Chuo Girls' High School|ja|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Chuo Girls' High School|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 栃木県立宇都宮中央高等学校|1=Tochigi Prefectural Utsunomiya Chuo High School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11535235}}社会部|date=1977-02-15|page=43|ref={{sfnref|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977}}}} === Related Articles === * {{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City}} * 左から {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Haruna-yama}}, {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|1=Otokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11578139}}, {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24887668}}, {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}, {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, 482m Peak, {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. 手前の緑は {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}} と {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Mount Tomatsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}。 |所在地 = {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}{{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City}} |最高峰 = {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}} |標高 = 561.6 }} {{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa (Tone River system)|1=Tagawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576724}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa River|en|Kinugawa River|WD=Q1042040|lt=Kinugawa}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Alps|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 篠井富屋連峰|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Futarasan shrine|en|Futarasan shrine|WD=Q701927|lt=Nikkō Futarasan Shrine}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|en|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountains|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日光の社寺|1=Shrines and Temples of Nikkō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1063133}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chausu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asama-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi–Tomiya Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Mount Tomatsuri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin-yama|1=Mount Myōjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11512579}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahera-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|en|Maruyama|WD=Q1739153|lt=Maruyama}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōshitsu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 高館山|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Mount Myōken|en|Mount Myōken|WD=Q868348|lt=Myoken-yama}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|en|Tōhoku Expressway|WD=Q428428|lt=Tohoku Expressway}} and {{ill|Japan National Route 293|en|Japan National Route 293|WD=Q6157155|lt=National Route 293}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|1=Kasamatsuyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11599914}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raiden-yama|1=Raiden-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11660213}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torami-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|1=Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q99484649}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q24887668}} (561.6 m) ** {{ill|Otokoyama|ja|男山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otokoyama|1=Otokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11578139}} (527 m) ** {{ill|Mount Haruna|en|Mount Haruna|WD=Q1191690|lt=Haruna-yama}} (524 m) ** {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}} (501 m) * Tomiya Range ** {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}} (476.6 m) ** {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (412 m) ** {{ill|Oniyama|ja|鬼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oniyama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}} (372 m) ** {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|1=Kasamatsuyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11599914}} (327.8 m) ** {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (409 m) ** {{ill|Mount Myōken|en|Mount Myōken|WD=Q868348|lt=Myoken-yama}} (320 m) == Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountain system|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Hills|qq=}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|en|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|WD=Q10946254|lt=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|1=Hanawada Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11428387}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chigato Shrine|1=Chigata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q98526762}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takao Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Atago Shrine in {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City}} located to the northwest of the range. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=[[栃木県立博物館|ja|栃木県立博物館]] 編|title=こんなにあるよ!とちぎの鉱物 ～鉱山と鉱物のものがたり～|date=2014-07-19|publisher={{ill|Tochigi Prefectural Museum|en|Tochigi Prefectural Museum|WD=Q11535226|lt=Tochigi Prefectural Museum}}|series=第109回企画展|page=80|isbn=978-4-88758-077-0|ref={{sfnref|栃木県立博物館 編|2014}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|title=地域総合調査報告 篠井|publisher={{ill|Utsunomiya Chuo Girls' High School|ja|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Chuo Girls' High School|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 栃木県立宇都宮中央高等学校|1=Tochigi Prefectural Utsunomiya Chuo High School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11535235}}社会部|date=1977-02-15|page=43|ref={{sfnref|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977}}}} === Related Articles === * {{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City}} * Prefecture}}. On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa (Tone River system)|1=Tagawa River (Tone River System)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576724}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa River|en|Kinugawa River|WD=Q1042040|lt=Kinugawa|1=Kinugawa River}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Alps|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 篠井富屋連峰|1=Shinoi-Tomiya Range|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture|1=Tochigi Prefecture}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Futarasan shrine|en|Futarasan shrine|WD=Q701927|lt=Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|1=Futarasan shrine}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|en|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikkō Tōshō-gū|1=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountains|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日光の社寺|1=Shrines and Temples of Nikkō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1063133}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chausu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asama-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi-Tomiya Range|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Tomatsuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin-yama|1=Mount Myōjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11512579}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahera-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City|1=Nikkō}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|en|Maruyama|WD=Q1739153|lt=Maruyama|1=Maruyama}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōshitsu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 高館山|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Mount Myōken|en|Mount Myōken|WD=Q868348|lt=Myoken-yama|1=Mount Myōken}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|en|Tōhoku Expressway|WD=Q428428|lt=Tohoku Expressway|1=Tōhoku Expressway}} and {{ill|Japan National Route 293|en|Japan National Route 293|WD=Q6157155|lt=National Route 293|1=Japan National Route 293}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|1=Kasamatsuyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11599914}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raiden-yama|1=Raiden-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11660213}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torami-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City|1=Nikkō}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|1=Q99484649|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q99484649}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountain system|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Hills|qq=}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|en|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|WD=Q10946254|lt=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|1=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|1=Hanawada Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on Shrine|ja|高尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takao Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi-Tomiya Range|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Tomatsuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin-yama|1=Mount Myōjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11512579}}. The highest peak of the Shinoi Tomiya Range is {{ill|Honzan|ja|本山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Honzan|lt_ja=本山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Honzan|1=Honzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520168}}, with an elevation of 561.6 m. To the north of Honzan lies {{ill|Takahera-yama|ja|高へら山|lt=Takahera-yama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahera-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, beyond which, separated by a flat area and straddling the border of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City|1=Nikkō}}, are {{ill|Maruyama|en|Maruyama|WD=Q1739153|lt=Maruyama|1=Maruyama}} (326.2 m) and {{ill|Dōshitsu-yama|ja|堂室山|lt=Dōshitsu-yama|lt_ja=堂室山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dōshitsu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (305.9 m). On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 高館山|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Mount Myōken|en|Mount Myōken|WD=Q868348|lt=Myoken-yama|1=Mount Myōken}}. Continuing southward from there are {{ill|Kurodo-yama|ja|黒戸山|lt=Kurodo-yama|lt_ja=黒戸山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kurodo-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Kabuto-yama|ja|兜山|lt=Kabuto-yama|lt_ja=兜山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabuto-yama|1=Kabuto-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11388843}}, and to the south, separated by the {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|en|Tōhoku Expressway|WD=Q428428|lt=Tohoku Expressway|1=Tōhoku Expressway}} and {{ill|Japan National Route 293|en|Japan National Route 293|WD=Q6157155|lt=National Route 293|1=Japan National Route 293}}, is {{ill|Kasamatsuyama|ja|笠松山|lt=Kasamatsuyama|lt_ja=笠松山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsuyama|1=Kasamatsuyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11599914}} (327.8 m). On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raiden-yama|1=Raiden-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11660213}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torami-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City|1=Nikkō}}. The entire Shinoi–Tomiya Range once served as the site of the {{ill|Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|ja|篠井金山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Kanayama (Tomiya Mine)|1=Q99484649|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q99484649}} (Tomiya Mine), where gold and copper were historically extracted.{{sfn|栃木県立宇都宮中央女子高等学校社会部|1977|p=32}}{{sfn|栃木県立博物館 編|2014|p=56}} == Major Peaks == * Shinoi Range ** Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountain system|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Hills|qq=}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|en|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|WD=Q10946254|lt=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|1=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|1=Hanawada Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11428387}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chigato Shrine|1=Chigata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q98526762}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takao Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City|1=Utsunomiya}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture|1=Tochigi On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa (Tone River system)|1=Tagawa River (Tone River System)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576724}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa River|en|Kinugawa River|WD=Q1042040|lt=Kinugawa|1=Kinugawa River}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Alps|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 篠井富屋連峰|1=Shinoi-Tomiya Range|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture|1=Tochigi Prefecture}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Futarasan shrine|en|Futarasan shrine|WD=Q701927|lt=Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|1=Futarasan shrine}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|en|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikkō Tōshō-gū|1=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountains|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日光の社寺|1=Shrines and Temples of Nikkō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1063133}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chausu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asama-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi-Tomiya Range|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Tomatsuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin-yama|1=Mount Myōjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11512579}}. On the southern side of Honzan, the range continues with {{ill|Iimori-yama|ja|飯盛山|lt=Iimori-yama|lt_ja=飯盛山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iimori-yama|1=Iimori-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11666630}}; further to the southeast is {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高舘山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高舘山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 高館山|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, from which, heading northeast, the range extends to {{ill|Yagura-yama|ja|矢倉山|lt=Yagura-yama|lt_ja=矢倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, while a low peak to the east leads to {{ill|Mount Myōken|en|Mount Myōken|WD=Q868348|lt=Myoken-yama|1=Mount Myōken}}. On the west side of {{ill|Takamata-yama|ja|高館山|lt=Takamata-yama|lt_ja=高館山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamata-yama|1=Mount Takadate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11673281}}, there is {{ill|Raiden-yama|ja|雷電山|lt=Raiden-yama|lt_ja=雷電山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raiden-yama|1=Raiden-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11660213}} (368 m), and to its northwest, {{ill|Torami-yama|ja|寅巳山|lt=Torami-yama|lt_ja=寅巳山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torami-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (458.8 m) appears, after which the range connects with the Asama-yama of {{ill|Nikkō|en|Nikkō|WD=Q235753|lt=Nikkō City|1=Nikkō}}. Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountain system|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Hills|qq=}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|en|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|WD=Q10946254|lt=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|1=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|1=Hanawada Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on Shrine|ja|高尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takao Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|36.68922|139.83536}}|caption=Location of Honzan|width=256}} '''Shinoi Tomiya Range''' (篠井富屋連峰, しのいとみやれんぽう) is the collective name for the mountain area that forms the northern mountain system of {{ill|Utsunomiya|en|Utsunomiya|WD=Q200589|lt=Utsunomiya City|1=Utsunomiya}} in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture|1=Tochigi On its southeast side flows the {{ill|Tagawa (Tone River system)|ja|田川 (利根川水系)|lt=Tagawa|lt_ja=田川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagawa (Tone River system)|1=Tagawa River (Tone River System)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576724}}, and on its northwest side the {{ill|Kinugawa River|en|Kinugawa River|WD=Q1042040|lt=Kinugawa|1=Kinugawa River}} runs, thereby forming a mountainous area sandwiched between the two rivers. This range is also sometimes called the {{ill|Utsunomiya Alps|ja|宇都宮アルプス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Alps|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 篠井富屋連峰|1=Shinoi-Tomiya Range|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}. == Overview == The northwestern mountain system of {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture|1=Tochigi Prefecture}} stretches from the area within the {{ill|Futarasan shrine|en|Futarasan shrine|WD=Q701927|lt=Nikkō Futarasan Shrine|1=Futarasan shrine}} and {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|en|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|WD=Q696641|lt=Nikkō Tōshō-gū|1=Nikkō Tōshō-gū}} enshrined within the {{ill|Nikkō Mountains|ja|日光山内|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountains|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日光の社寺|1=Shrines and Temples of Nikkō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1063133}}, continuing through {{ill|Ogura-yama|ja|小倉山 (日光市)|lt=Ogura-yama|lt_ja=小倉山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogura-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Atago-yama|ja|愛宕山 (日光市)|lt=Atago-yama|lt_ja=愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Chausu-yama|ja|茶臼山 (日光市)|lt=Chausu-yama|lt_ja=茶臼山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chausu-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Asama-yama|ja|浅間山 (日光市)|lt=Asama-yama|lt_ja=浅間山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asama-yama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}; then, in the northern part of Utsunomiya City, the range continues as the {{ill|Shinoi Tomiya Range|ja|篠井富屋連峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoi Tomiya Range|1=Shinoi-Tomiya Range|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11603531}}, and further on to the urban area with peaks such as {{ill|Tomesai-yama|ja|戸祭山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomesai-yama|1=Tomatsuri-yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11496593}}, {{ill|Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|ja|八幡山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Hachimanyama|lt_ja=八幡山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman-yama (Utsunomiya)|1=Mount Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390954}}, and {{ill|Myōjin-yama|ja|明神山 (宇都宮市)|lt=Myōjin-yama|lt_ja=明神山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin-yama|1=Mount Myōjin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11512579}}. Surroundings == The Shinoi–Tomiya Range is situated between the {{ill|Nikkō Mountain system|ja|日光山系|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Mountain system|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and the {{ill|Utsunomiya Hills|ja|宇都宮丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsunomiya Hills|qq=}}. This mountainous area has long been an object of mountain worship; numerous temples and shrines such as {{ill|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|en|Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|WD=Q10946254|lt=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine|1=Utsunomiya Futarayama Shrine}}, {{ill|Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|ja|塙田八幡宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanawada Hachiman Shrine|1=Hanawada Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11428387}}, {{ill|Chigato Shrine|ja|智賀都神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chigato Shrine|1=Chigata Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q98526762}}, {{ill|Takao Shrine|ja|高尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takao Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Yakushi-dō, and Dainichi Daikongen-dō have been established in the area, with additional shrines such as the
